seg_membrane_chord_score — EMPROOF suspect op

• Data kinds: labels2d × image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, membrane, tau: 'float' = 0.2, band: 'int' = 4, min_area: 'int' = 1500, min_segment: 'int' = 20, normalize: 'bool' = True, ignore_zero: 'bool' = True, max_points: 'int' = 400, min_hole: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import emproof; emproof.seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, membrane, tau: 'float' = 0.2, band: 'int' = 4, min_area: 'int' = 1500, min_segment: 'int' = 20, normalize: 'bool' = True, ignore_zero: 'bool' = True, max_points: 'int' = 400, min_hole: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsemproof.get("seg_membrane_chord_score"))

Usage

Suspected merge: length of the membrane "chord" crossing the interior of a label / diameter of the label. One row per label (connected component).

Procedure: inside a component (deeper than band px from the boundary), pixels with membrane response > tau are grouped into 8-connected components; for each membrane component of at least min_segment px, it is thickened by 3 px and the largest distance between 2 points among the pixels touching the boundary band (band < distance ≤ band + 3) is taken as the chord length. score = max chord length / sqrt(area). A membrane joining 2 places on the boundary (= the border between 2 cells stuck together) has score ≈ 1; fragments that do not touch the boundary give 0 or small values. Membrane components with holes (holes of at least min_hole px = closed rings = mitochondria, vesicles) are excluded from the chord candidates -- a ring touching 2 points of the boundary has the same "2 distant points" as a chord, so they are separated first by whether they have a hole. Membranes whose ring is broken into an arc cannot be excluded (the main reason AUC does not reach 1 on real data).

On CREMI sample A (512² sections, 12 slices, prototype), artificially merged components vs the rest: AUC 0.83 (tau 0.2).

Columns: label / component / area / score / chord_px / n_segments / cy / cx (descending by score). Components smaller than min_area are not counted (the chord of a small fragment is about its diameter and always comes out high).

>>> table = seg_membrane_chord_score(labels, seg_membrane_response(raw))

>>> table["label"][:5], table["score"][:5] # most suspicious first
